about.hero.title: About
about.hero.statement: GitHub has enough projects. What is missing is direction.
about.hero.description: We organize popular repos, topics, languages, and project relationships into visual maps so you can find results and understand where to go next.
about.features.title: Core features
about.features.description: Search is only the starting point. We organize project relationships, contributor rankings, and distribution views so you can decide faster what to save, compare, or explore next.
about.features.graph.title: Network graph
about.features.graph.description: Start from one repo and branch out to similar projects, topics, and languages to understand the technical landscape faster.
about.features.graph.fit: Best for: digging deeper from strong projects
about.features.learning.title: Learning map
about.features.learning.description: We turn repos in the dataset into readable learning paths so you can pick a topic first and then go deeper into the most representative projects.
about.features.learning.fit: Best for: people unsure what to learn first
about.features.rankings.title: Rankings
about.features.rankings.description: See owner and language distribution first, understand the broader trend, and then decide where to look next.
about.features.rankings.fit: Best for: getting the big picture first
about.features.scatter.title: Scatterplot
about.features.scatter.description: Use the distribution of stars and forks to quickly separate popular, technical, and worth-comparing repos.
about.features.scatter.fit: Best for: comparing popularity and adoption
about.next.title: Ready to begin?
about.next.description: If you already know what you want, go back to the homepage and start searching. If you want to organize your direction first, open the learning map.
collection.hero.title: Jump straight into curated learning paths from 666 repos
collection.hero.description: This page is not another search result. It organizes the dataset into readable topic paths first, so you can pick a direction before diving into the most representative repos.
collection.overview.title: Pick a path, then go deeper
collection.overview.description: Representative repos are grouped by learning direction so you do not have to guess where to begin from 666 entries.
collection.overview.summary: {pathCount} learning paths organized from {repoCount} repos. Choose a direction first, then open the representative projects.
collection.overview.empty.title: No learning paths available yet
collection.overview.empty.description: Make sure /api/tools returns data correctly, then refresh the page.

collection.detail.empty.title: No path selected yet
collection.detail.empty.description: Pick a learning map card above and the representative repos, role labels, and reasons will appear here.

collection.reason.stars: High stars make it a strong representative example
collection.reason.default: This repo scores highly for “{title}”, making it a good {role} to review

collection.path.frontend.title: Frontend and Web UI
collection.path.frontend.description: Best when you want to start with UI, interaction, dashboards, and the way products are presented on the web.
collection.path.frontend.audience: Good for people who want to break down interfaces and frontend implementation details
collection.path.python.title: Python and Automation
collection.path.python.description: Build practical intuition through Python scripts, tools, and automation-focused projects.
collection.path.python.audience: Good for people who want to build quick tools and automation with Python
collection.path.ai.title: AI / LLM / Agent
collection.path.ai.description: Focuses on LLMs, agents, and AI workflows for understanding how modern AI applications are assembled.
collection.path.ai.audience: Good for people who want a fast overview of agents, RAG, and LLM applications
collection.path.data.title: Data Science and Machine Learning
collection.path.data.description: Organizes data analysis, model implementation, and deep learning examples into an easier learning sequence.
collection.path.data.audience: Good for people who want to move from data handling into models and real implementations
collection.path.devtools.title: Developer Tools and CLI
collection.path.devtools.description: Groups tooling, terminal, and workflow repos into a practical path focused on engineering efficiency.
collection.path.devtools.audience: Good for people who want to improve workflow efficiency and understand tool design
collection.path.opensource.title: Open Source Beginner-Friendly Projects
collection.path.opensource.description: Highlights repos that are easier to read, intentionally educational, or more approachable for first-time open source readers.
collection.path.opensource.audience: Good for people just starting to read open source repos and unsure where to begin
collection.path.curated.title: Awesome / Curated Resources
collection.path.curated.description: If you are not sure which single project to learn first, curated resource lists are often the fastest way to find direction.
collection.path.curated.audience: Good for people who want to scan resource lists before choosing what to dive into
collection.path.build.title: Build-your-own / Learning-by-building
collection.path.build.description: Great for learning by rebuilding things yourself, from imitation to reconstruction to understanding the underlying ideas.
collection.path.build.audience: Good for people who like learning by doing and strengthening skills through rebuilding

graph.detail.color.title: How color is determined
graph.detail.color.description: The default teal palette splits repos currently on screen into five star tiers. More popular repos appear darker with stronger outlines. Turn on language coloring to group other nodes by language instead.
graph.detail.distance.title: How distance is determined
graph.detail.distance.description: The closer two nodes are, the more similar the repos are. The system looks at shared topics first, then adds signals from matching language, owner, and description keywords.
